report_prompt.role: You are a sales-analytics analyst. Build a PDF report on which sales teams and callers performed best on the target day in terms of converting potential clients into enrolled customers. Anyone, including a reader with no analytics background, must be able to understand it: a one-page summary first, then thorough sections with charts and plain-language explanations of what each figure means. Use only the data sources, definitions and format below. Do not invent or substitute definitions. Where a parameter cannot be met, stop and state which parameter failed and why.

preflight.step: Run from the repository root with PYTHONPATH=. and install requirements.txt with pip.
Confirm LEADSQUARED_ACCESS_KEY, LEADSQUARED_SECRET_KEY and SALESA_API_KEY are set. Never print their values.
Run `python -m integrations.leadsquared check`. If it fails, stop and report the error.
Write all fetched data under the git-ignored data/ folder. Make no repository commits.
The whole run is one command: `python -m analytics.team_performance TARGET_DATE`. It fetches, validates, and only then renders.

scope.param: Target day 00:00:00–23:59:59 IST = previous day 18:30:00 to target day 18:29:59 UTC.

Show every time in IST. LeadSquared CreatedOn is UTC and is the call start; never use a call note's StartTime. A transcript takes its time from its matched LeadSquared call, because API clocks can be 5 h 30 min off.
Target day through target day + 3 days (IST), capped at now. Print it on the report.

sources.source: LeadSquared activities, event 22 (outbound) and 21 (inbound), parsed with parse_phone_call and read with iter_activities_started (edits up to 3 days past the day, kept by CreatedOn, because the API filters on ModifiedOn). Never use lead edits or "leads modified" as calls.
"Zipteams Notes", event 237, created in the window or in the 2 hours after it (read with the same 3-day edit margin as S1). Required: a report without it is invalid.
Leads in ProspectStage "Course Enrolled" plus stage-change history (event 3002), following the first-time-enrollment logic in scripts/d1_backfill.py.
"Payment Successful", event 213. Report the count only.

team_mapping.param: Match a call to a user by user_id, then by exact caller full name.

Team = the first group in MemberOfGroups, in LeadSquared's order, that is not a calling-software group (a name containing the word Acefone or Mcube, any case: "Acefone Users", "Mcube Users", "New Joinees - Mcube"; groups for the phone system, not sales teams). Use analytics.definitions.team_of. Each caller is in exactly one team; a caller with only calling-software groups is Unassigned.

Groups that share callers: section 3 also lists every group with at least one dialling caller whose team is another group, calling-software groups included (marked "phone system", listed first), each caller counted in every group they belong to: Callers, Of them counted in another team, Dials, Answer rate, Dials failed, Real conversations, Leads reached, Enrolled (credited), Conversion, and the 3 groups its callers most share. Rows overlap and are never added up or ranked. A "What this means" note compares the phone systems' answer and failed rates with the day's and names the group with the most callers counted in another team. Section 1 explains what a team is; section 11 counts the callers listed under a phone system first and in more than one group; the appendix names each caller's other groups.
No group → "Unassigned". Caller not a LeadSquared user → "Not a user". Show both in totals; never rank them.
Rank only teams with at least 3 callers and at least 25 real conversations.
Exclude automated welcome, reminder and webinar bots from all figures.

calling_metrics.metric: Outbound with status "Answered" ÷ dials, percentage to 1 decimal.
Any call with status "Answered" and duration ≥ 120 s.
Distinct lead_id with at least one real conversation.
Sum of answered call durations ÷ 60, rounded.
Distinct callers with at least one outbound call.

Across all calls of the day (including Unassigned and Not a user): calls, answered calls (inbound and outbound), real conversations, leads reached, credited enrollments, credited ÷ leads reached, and how many credited leads are among the leads reached (credit follows any answered call, so a lead can enrol after a call shorter than 2 minutes). Descriptive only.

Per IST hour from the first to the last hour with calls (an empty hour between them shows 0 and "–"): dials, answered dials and their share, real conversations and inbound calls. Name the best and worst answer-rate hours only among hours with at least 2% of the day's dials. Draw the hour table in blocks of 12 hours.
calling_metrics.forbidden: Do not define "connected" by lead stage, lead edits or owner counts.

conversion_metrics.metric: The lead's FIRST ever stage change to "Course Enrolled", timestamped inside the conversion window. A lead that already sits in an enrolled stage is not an enrollment.
Credit each enrollment to the caller with the most answered talk time on that lead on the target day. A lead with no target-day conversation is not credited.
Credited enrollments ÷ leads reached, percentage to 1 decimal.
Enrollments timestamped on the target day, by the lead owner's team. Context only.
Mark teams that mainly call bootcamp registrants or post-enrolment leads (currently Elite Changemakers and the DSV teams) as "warm leads" in the table.
Enrollments in the conversion window by IST day, split into credited (P28) and not credited.

zipteams_metrics.metric: Credit each note to the caller of the lead's last answered call at or before the note's CreatedOn, and keep its analysis on that call (per call in data/report_{D}/zip_calls.csv). Drop and count notes with no such call. A note written after the day counts only if it lands within 5 minutes of the end of one of the day's calls; count the rest separately.
(HIGH + MODERATE) ÷ notes rated, where mx_Custom_1 is not NOT_AVAILABLE.
zipteams_metrics.rule: Show "–" for teams with no notes. Never treat a missing score as 0.

transcripts.rule: At most 10 numbers per request, at most 9 requests per client run, at most 10 requests per minute: wait at least 7 s between requests and 60 s after earlier calls. Use max_retries=0 and catch errors per chunk.

Sample up to 90 leads: up to 40 converted (P27/P28, longest target-day call first) and up to 50 non-converted with an answered call of 300 s or more, 10 at random (seed 5) from each of the 5 ranked teams with the most real conversations.

Keep only transcripts that match one of the lead's target-day LeadSquared calls (same number, start within 10 minutes, a 5 h 30 min shift allowed when durations agree within 10%); print how many needed the shift. Per lead, analyse the longest transcript of 120 s or more.

Report the % of converted vs non-converted calls containing each marker (case-insensitive regex): price/fee/EMI; discount/scholarship/offer; payment step (payment link, pay now, balance payment); urgency (deadline, seats, last date); discovery questions; batch/LMS/onboarding; career/ROI; fixed next step (date or time).
At most 3 short quotes, each tied to a named caller and team. Never include customer phone numbers or names.

ranking.rule: Sort eligible teams by credited enrollments, then conversion rate, then real conversations.
Name the best team, a runner-up, and the best non-warm front-line team.

Recognise up to 9 callers: 8 sorted by credited enrollments, then real conversations, then talk minutes, then name, plus one coaching case: the caller with the most real conversations (then talk minutes, then name) among callers with at most 1 credited enrollment and at least 1 real conversation, team not Unassigned, no dialer issue (P52b) and not already recognised.

Callers who need support: up to 5 callers chosen like the P52 coaching case, which comes first. Generate the note from their figures: their real conversations and enrollments, any with most of their long calls flagged (P71), and how many more callers tie with the last one listed.
Dialer issue: a caller with 20+ dials of which 50%+ ended in CallFailure. List them so the dialer is fixed before the caller is judged.

Coaching assets: up to 4 callers with at least 15 Zipteams notes, sorted by probing + pitch + objection, then name, headed "Good questioning and explaining". The note names any with no credited enrollment (their calls teach questioning, not closing) and any also in P52a.

output.rule: PDF, A4 portrait, no page limit: a one-page summary, then as many pages as the sections and the caller table need. Saved as /mnt/project-files/reports/team_calling_report_{TARGET_DATE}.pdf.

Render HTML with headless Chromium (--print-to-pdf --no-pdf-header-footer), with "Page N of M", the day and the version in each footer. Render the summary alone too: it must come to exactly 1 page; if not, draw fewer ranked teams on page 1 (15, then 12, 10, 8, 5, 3; the rest stay in section 3). Cut team names on page 1 after 32 characters. If meta.json carries a "sample" note (a layout sample from part of a day), show it in a page-1 banner and write "SAMPLE, partial data" in every footer; a normal run never sets it.

Page 1, the summary, readable in a minute: title with weekday and date, the conversion window and when the data was read; the day as 5 connected steps (P23a); what happened (best team, runner-up, best front-line team, busiest teams, the biggest gap or tied gaps in the P33 sample, with call counts); Teams ranked (conversion bar, enrolled, real conversations); Callers to recognise (P52, incl. the coaching case); What to do next (fix the phones first when any caller has a dialer issue, then the payment step, a full pitch and the coaching case). Then: 1. How to read this report; 2. From calls to enrolments (P23a, P29d); 3. Teams and groups compared (P63, teams not ranked, groups that share callers P11a); 4. Weak spots of the day; 5. Team by team (one card per ranked team with one suggested next step); 6. Callers (P52, P52a, P52b, P53); 7. What the converting calls had in common (P33); 8. Call quality scores (Zipteams); 9. When the calls happened (P24a); 10. Calls to review (P74); 11. How this report was made and checked (method and every validation check); Appendix: every caller, by team.

Plain language for readers who are not analysts: explain every term in section 1; give sections 2, 3, 6, 7, 8 and 9 a "What this means" note generated from the figures, and sections 4 and 5 what to do for each finding and each team; write conversion as enrolments per 100 leads reached, never as a share of them; generate every sentence from the figures, handling ties, single teams, zero and missing values; put every chart's numbers on its marks or in a table, never rely on colour alone, show "–" for no data, and never show customer names or numbers.

Scorecard columns. Section 3: Team, Callers, Dials, Answer rate, Real conversations, Leads reached, Talk minutes, Enrolled (credited), Conversion, Enrolled on the day (owner's team, P29b); then the group table (P11a). Section 8: calls checked, Asked about needs (probing), Explained the course fully (pitch), Answered concerns well (objection handling), Lead's interest high or moderate (intent); ranked teams first, then the others under a divider.
Low answer rate: a team's answer rate below 70% of the day's (all dials; the same 70% as the lagging-caller rule). Used only in the words of section 4 and the team cards, never in the ranking.

Section 11 must state: the conversion window, the enrollment and credit definitions, the Zipteams coverage gap, the team-mapping rule with the count of callers listed under a phone system first and of multi-group callers, the warm-lead flag, the validation summary with every check's result, and "Parameters v1.5". Section 1 explains the window, the enrollment and credit definitions, the warm-lead flag and what a team is (P11, P11a) in plain words.
Compute the weekday from the date. Never write it from memory.
Make no repository commits or pushes without the owner's approval.

call_integrity.note: v1.2; every flag means needs review, never proof. Calibrated on 5 Oct 2026: 1,450 eligible calls; 90-call transcript sample, median 148 words a minute.
call_integrity.rule: Find answered calls of 2+ minutes by LeadSquared users that may be fake, artificially stretched, or long with little or no conversation, and the callers with the most of them. A flag is a prompt to listen to the recording.
Overlap: an answered call starts more than 30 s before the same caller's previous answered call ends; flag both if 2+ minutes.
Repeat: 3 or more real conversations between the same caller and lead on the day.
Just over 2 minutes: a caller with 10+ eligible calls whose share of 120–149 s calls is at least twice the day's account-wide share; flag those calls.
Per caller: eligible calls, flagged calls, flagged share, transcripts checked. Rank only callers with 10+ eligible calls, by flagged share.

Transcripts: no content under 30 words; thin under 60 words a minute; recorded message, IVR, voicemail or hold text in the first 40 words; loop when one 3-word phrase is 15%+ of the words. No speaker labels or timestamps exist, so words a minute stands in for silence and the customer's share is not measured.

Transcript sample in its own run (`python -m analytics.call_integrity TARGET_DATE [--limit N]`, API limits apply): a third calls flagged by P68–P70, a third each caller's longest call, the rest 120–149 s calls. Match on the same number, closest start within 10 minutes; a 5 h 30 min shift also counts when durations agree within 10% (some API times carry the wrong timezone).

Section 10 "Calls to review": flagged counts by signal, transcript coverage, up to 5 ranked callers with flagged/eligible calls. Per-call evidence to data/report_{TARGET_DATE}/integrity_calls.csv. No lead names or numbers in any output.

validation.check: The total S1 call count is printed and equals the sum of all team dials and inbound calls, including Unassigned and Not a user.
Zipteams notes attributed ÷ total is printed, and fewer than 5% were dropped.
Every team figure quoted in page 1's "what happened" appears in the team tables (section 3).
The summary, rendered alone, fits on exactly 1 page.
"Parameters v1.5" is printed in section 11, which lists every check with its result.
No duplicate call or Zipteams activity IDs.
Every call and Zipteams note falls inside the target IST day, and no call has a start time that cannot be read.
Calls from callers who are not LeadSquared users stay under 5%.
Each enrollment is counted once, and every credited caller had an answered call with that lead on the target day.
Every rate is within 0–100 and no call has a negative duration.

Totals reconcile: fetched = counted + other-day + unreadable-time + bot calls; calls = team dials + inbound; credited = sum of team credited = sum of their callers; Zipteams attributed + dropped = total.
A seeded sample of 10 credited enrollments is re-read from LeadSquared stage history and confirmed as first-ever "Course Enrolled" in the window.
Call-integrity counts reconcile (flagged and checked calls never exceed eligible calls; caller totals add up) and carry no lead details.
Every P62 section is in the report, in order.

Callers in more than one group: each caller's team is one of their own groups and never a calling-software group, or Unassigned when they have no other group; every group that shares a dialling caller with another team is in section 3, and its dials, inbound calls, real conversations and credited enrolments equal the sums over its callers.

report_prompt.deliverable: The PDF at the P60 path, plus a 5-line chat summary: the best team with its conversion rate, the runner-up, the top 3 callers, the single biggest gap found, and any parameter that could not be met.
